paragraphs: DebrisTech documents the removal of storm debris so the entities paying for cleanup can claim reimbursement from FEMA. The customers are governments, and the site asks any government entity seeking the service to fill in a contact form.

The work runs on a custom Electronic Debris Management System that keeps a cradle-to-grave digital record of a recovery from start to finish. In place of handwritten tickets, monitors carry real-time data collection devices, which the company presents as a gain in documentation, accuracy and security. The company places what it sells under Category A debris removal expenses.

By its own count, the firm has monitored the removal of more than 50 million cubic yards of debris. The same tally credits 80 debris removal projects completed in the last two years alone. Those projects reach across 17 states and territories.

quote.text: We document the removal of debris to aid entities in getting their maximum reimbursement from FEMA.
